name: Laubressel
summary: The allied army of Bohemia followed up its success at Bar-sur-Aube and beat Macdonald and Oudinot again at Laubressel, east of Troyes.

forces.name: Duhesme's Division
forces.summary: Gérard's division at the bridge of La Guillotière on the Barse, which held it until it was turned and lost two guns and four hundred men.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
Gérard's corps isn't on Nafziger's return of 2 March; it is from his return of the II Corps on 12 March, nine days after Laubressel.
Its twelve battalions had twenty to three hundred and fifty men each, 1,900 or so in all; each regiment is shown as one battalion at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
The corps' artillery, four foot companies and a horse company, is one with each division here.
Brigades of six regiments, where the list's take three, and three light regiments, where it allows one in the division, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Hamelinaye's Division
forces.summary: Gérard's other division, linking Duhesme's to Rottembourg's. Bellair's brigade was routed; Jarry's covered Duhesme's left and drew off in order, and Gérard fell back into Troyes.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
Gérard's corps isn't on Nafziger's return of 2 March; it is from his return of the II Corps on 12 March, nine days after Laubressel.

Nafziger names it Hamelinaye's or Dufour's division. Its thirteen battalions had fifty to two hundred men each, some 1,600 in all; each regiment is shown as one battalion at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
The corps' artillery is one company with each division here.
Brigades of eight and five regiments, where the list's take three, and four light regiments, where it allows one in the division, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

missing.name: 22/8th, 17/5th and 2/9th Foot and 6/3rd Horse Artillery
missing.reason: The rest of Gérard's corps artillery.

forces.name: Rottembourg's Division
forces.summary: Oudinot's Young Guard on the plateau of Laubressel, which held it until Wittgenstein's Russians came round its flank and forced it back.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Nafziger's return of Macdonald's army before Troyes on 2 March, from Koch's history and the French archives; its strengths are of 1 to 10 March.
Its regiments were newly raised that winter, largely of conscripts under a cadre of veterans; they are the list's Young Guard, as it rates them.

The division had some seven hundred men in ten battalions by 5 March; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all. Its regiments are voltigeurs now, where at La Rothière they were tirailleurs.
Its foot company, five 6-pdrs and two howitzers, is with Baudin's brigade.
Regiments of three battalions, where the list's take two, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Leval's Division
forces.summary: Veterans from Spain, the strongest division of Oudinot's corps, which fell back on Troyes with it as Wittgenstein turned the plateau.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's return of Macdonald's army before Troyes on 2 March, from Koch's history and the French archives; its strengths are of 1 to 10 March.

The division had some 5,800 men in seventeen battalions, three to nine hundred each. Nafziger gives Chassé's brigade as its third on 5 March, and as the 9th Division's on 1 March; Wikipedia's account has Chassé leading a division.
Its foot company of eight 6-pdrs and four howitzers is its divisional artillery, and the 9th Division's company is in its reserve.
Brigades of four regiments, where the list's take three, and three light regiments, where it allows one in the division, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Pacthod's National Guards
forces.summary: National Guards raised that winter in the departments, which marched with Oudinot's corps and fell back on Troyes with it.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's return of Macdonald's army before Troyes on 2 March, from Koch's history and the French archives; its strengths are of 1 to 10 March.
Its National Guards, raised that winter from the departments, are shown as Line; the list's Wavering or Morale 5 would suit them better.
The division had some 3,900 men in five regiments, three to a thousand men each; each regiment is shown as one unit.
Its own foot company and the VII Corps' reserve companies are with it here; the reserve's horse company is left out.
With five units of infantry, the division's battery and its reserve batteries show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Albert's Division
forces.summary: Macdonald's corps, which fell back on Troyes without being pressed while Oudinot's and Gérard's were beaten.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's return of Macdonald's army before Troyes on 2 March, from Koch's history and the French archives; its strengths are of 1 to 10 March.

The division had some 3,200 men; the regiments of Brest and Rochefort, National Guards of the naval ports, had three to eight hundred a battalion. Its National Guards, raised that winter from the departments, are shown as Line; the list's Wavering or Morale 5 would suit them better.
The XI Corps' cavalry, two squadrons of the 13th Hussars, is with the division here.
With six battalions, the second foot battery shows as a historical departure; the division's horse company is left out.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Amey's Division
forces.summary: A small division of Macdonald's corps, which fell back on Troyes without being pressed.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's return of Macdonald's army before Troyes on 2 March, from Koch's history and the French archives; its strengths are of 1 to 10 March.

The division had about seven hundred men in four battalions. The battalions of Calvados and La Manche were National Guards. Its National Guards, raised that winter from the departments, are shown as Line; the list's Wavering or Morale 5 would suit them better.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

missing.name: 6/4th Horse Artillery
missing.reason: Four 8-pdrs and a howitzer, with no cavalry in the division to allow them.

forces.name: Brayer's Division
forces.summary: The third division of Macdonald's corps, which fell back on Troyes without being pressed.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's return of Macdonald's army before Troyes on 2 March, from Koch's history and the French archives; its strengths are of 1 to 10 March.

The division had about 2,000 men in seven battalions; by the end of March they were Guye's brigade of Boyer de Rébeval's division at Paris. Its National Guards, raised that winter from the departments, are shown as Line; the list's Wavering or Morale 5 would suit them better.

Its three foot companies are one in its divisional artillery and two in its reserve; with seven battalions, where the list wants eight for each reserve battery, the two show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Saint-Germain's Cavalry
forces.summary: Maurin's light horse retook most of the artillery park Pahlen's cavalry had overrun at Thennelières.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's return of Macdonald's army before Troyes on 2 March, from Koch's history and the French archives; its strengths are of 1 to 10 March.

Maurin's 2nd Light Cavalry Division is Dommanget's and Jamin's brigades, and Delort's 2nd Cuirassier Division Blancard's and Sopransy's: the regiments of Sébastiani's corps of 1813, fifty to a hundred and fifty men each by now. Each is shown as one unit at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
The chevau-légers lanciers are the list's Lancers. Its two horse detachments are one in its divisional artillery and one in its reserve.
Light brigades of six and five regiments and a heavy brigade of four, where the list's take four and three, and two heavy brigades, where it takes one, show as historical departures.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Milhaud's Cavalry
forces.summary: Milhaud's corps, which fell back with the infantry without being engaged.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's return of Macdonald's army before Troyes on 2 March, from Koch's history and the French archives; its strengths are of 1 to 10 March.

Piré's light division, 1,421 men, is Subervie's and the second light brigades; Briche's dragoons, 1,700, Montélégier's and Ludot's; and L'Héritier's, 1,269, Lamotte's and Collaert's. Their regiments had a hundred to four hundred men; they are shown at full size.
Its three horse companies are one in its divisional artillery and one in its reserve, as the list takes them.
Four heavy cavalry brigades, where the list takes one, and more heavy cavalry than its half of the army for corps support, show as historical departures.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Trelliard's Dragoons
forces.formation: 5th Heavy Cavalry Division, VI Cavalry Corps (Kellermann)
forces.summary: Trelliard's dragoons from Spain, which counter-attacked the Russians at Thennelières.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's return of Macdonald's army before Troyes on 2 March, from Koch's history and the French archives; its strengths are of 1 to 10 March.
Its strengths are of 7 March: each regiment had three or four battalion-sized squadrons, a hundred to five hundred men in all; each is shown as one unit.
Its horse company is its divisional artillery.

Two heavy cavalry brigades, where the list takes one, more heavy cavalry than its half of the army for corps support, and a cavalry force with no infantry, show as historical departures. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Wrede's Austrians
forces.formation: Hardegg's and Splény's divisions, V Corps (Wrede)
forces.summary: Hardegg's Austrians, who led Wrede's corps towards Montiéramey while its guns opened the attack.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Austrian 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Wikipedia's order of battle for La Rothière, a month before; Laubressel's own order of battle gives the allied corps only by division.
Hardegg's 1st Division is Geramb's and Mengen's brigades, and Splény's 2nd Division the infantry, whose brigadier isn't known, and Minutillo's cavalry. They were the same regiments as at Hanau.

Regiments of four battalions, where the list takes two Large ones, one line brigade where the list wants two for the force's points, two advanced guard brigades, where it allows one, a cavalry battery with Minutillo's two regiments, where it wants three, and two position batteries with eight line battalions, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Rechberg's Division
forces.summary: Rechberg's Bavarians, who attacked towards Courteranges and Troyes.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Bavarian 1812 list, the nearest to 1814; Bavaria had joined the allies in October.
After Wikipedia's order of battle for La Rothière, a month before; Laubressel's own order of battle gives the allied corps only by division.

The Landwehr battalions, national field battalions raised from the districts' militia, are shown as Line. Brigades of single battalions of several regiments have more regiments than the list's brigade takes, which shows as a historical departure.

Each division's cavalry battery, light 6-pdrs with the gunners riding, is the list's Light Artillery, with its chevau-légers; its 6-pdr battery is its Foot Battery, and one of the corps' four 12-pdr batteries is with each division as its Position Battery.

The 1st Line's battalion in Maillot's brigade is unnumbered in the order of battle; it is shown as the third. Three chevau-léger regiments in Vieregg's brigade, where the list's takes two, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.summary: Beckers's Bavarians, with the rest of Wrede's corps in the advance on Troyes.

forces.summary: Lamotte's Bavarians, with the rest of Wrede's corps in the advance on Troyes.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Bavarian 1812 list, the nearest to 1814; Bavaria had joined the allies in October.

forces.name: The Crown Prince of Württemberg's Corps
forces.summary: About fifteen thousand Württembergers on the allied left: Prince Adam's cavalry stood idle, and Koch's and Döring's infantry followed Macdonald towards Sens.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Württemberg 1812 list, the nearest to 1814; Württemberg had joined the allies in November.
After Wikipedia's order of battle for La Rothière, a month before; Laubressel's own order of battle gives the allied corps only by division.
Koch's infantry division is the three infantry brigades, Prince Adam's cavalry division the two cavalry brigades.
The horse chasseur regiments are the list's Jäger zu Pferde, and the Crown Prince's dragoons its Chevau-légers.
Each foot battery, four 6-pdrs and two howitzers, is the list's Light Artillery.

Two cavalry brigades, where the list allows one for the infantry, three regiments in Döring's brigade and three light battalions in Stockmayer's, where the list's take two, and two foot batteries, where it allows one, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Gyulai's Corps
forces.summary: Gyulai's Austrians, about ten thousand, on the allied left, which attacked the French at Silvarouvres.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Austrian 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
After Wikipedia's order of battle for La Rothière, a month before; Laubressel's own order of battle gives the allied corps only by division.

Crenneville's light division is Haecht's and Trenck's brigades, Fresnel's Pflüger's and Csollich's, and Prince Hohenlohe's Splény's and Grimmer's. The St George Grenz regiment's two battalions are one with each of Crenneville's brigades.
The Mariassy and Ignaz Gyulai regiments, recruited in Hungary, are the list's Hungarian infantry.

Regiments of three and four battalions, where the list takes two Large ones, two advanced guard brigades, where it allows one, and four brigade batteries and two position batteries, where it allows three and one, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Gorchakov's Corps
forces.summary: Gorchakov's infantry, which attacked Laubressel and took the plateau.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
After Nafziger's return of the Army of Bohemia in January 1814; the corps was much weaker by the time of this battle.

Mezentsov's 5th Division (the first three brigades) and Helfreich's 14th (the last three), with a light and a position battery. Nafziger's Craonne and Laon returns give the Tula and Navaginsk regiments to Vorontsov's corps in March.
Four infantry brigades and two Jäger brigades, where the list allows three and one, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 3 of the 6 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Eugen of Württemberg's Corps
forces.summary: Eugen of Württemberg's infantry, which took Bouranton and attacked the slopes of Laubressel.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
After Nafziger's return of the Army of Bohemia in January 1814; the corps was much weaker by the time of this battle.

Prince Eugen of Württemberg, one of the list's named commanders, leads it. Shakhovsky's 3rd Division (the first three brigades) and Pyshnitsky's 4th (the last three), with a light and a position battery; the 4th Division's Jäger brigade has no named commander.
Four infantry brigades and two Jäger brigades, where the list allows three and one, show as historical departures.

Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named Major General Eugene von Württemberg, with his own rating; but 3 of the 6 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Pahlen's Cavalry
forces.summary: Pahlen's horse, which raided the French artillery park at Thennelières.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.
After Nafziger's return of the Army of Bohemia in January 1814; the corps was much weaker by the time of this battle.
Three light cavalry brigades, where the list allows one, and cavalry with no infantry brigade to allow it, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 2 of the 4 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

toCome.name: Jacquinot's Division
toCome.summary: Light horse that stampeded at La Chapelle-Saint-Luc; it isn't on Nafziger's return.
